name: Mark P Marron
current_role: President, CEO and Director, ePlus inc. (Herndon, Virginia)
profile: Mark Marron has run IT solutions provider ePlus since August 2016, after joining in 2005 as SVP of Sales and becoming COO in 2010. A 30+ year tech-sales veteran (NetIQ, Computer Associates), he leads a company that reported about $2.4B in fiscal-2026 net sales, increasingly focused on AI, data center and security services.
interesting_fact: Under Marron, ePlus was named Digital Realty's 2026 Americas Partner of the Year in recognition of its AI expertise, a direct data-center angle for the podcast.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a B.S. in Computer Science from Montclair State University and earlier was General Manager of Worldwide Channel Sales at Computer Associates before becoming SVP of Worldwide Sales and Services at NetIQ.

public_contacts.value: kparkhurst@eplus.com (Kley Parkhurst, SVP, ePlus media contact)

notes: Succeeded longtime CEO Bruce Norton in 2016. Best route is the ePlus corporate communications contact (Kley Parkhurst). Low personal media profile.

name: Jeffrey Jacobowitz
current_role: Founder and Managing Member, Simcoe Capital Management, LLC (New York); former director of Donnelley Financial Solutions (DFIN)
profile: Jeffrey Jacobowitz founded New York hedge fund Simcoe Capital Management in 2003 to invest in undervalued U.S. public companies with a concentrated, 3-5 year horizon. Simcoe built a ~7.9% stake in DFIN and he joined its board in 2019 under a cooperation agreement; he does not appear on DFIN's 2026 director slate.
interesting_fact: He joined DFIN's board via a 2019 settlement with his fund, having earlier served on the boards of Exar Corporation, Telular Corporation and Alloy Inc. as an activist-style shareholder representative.
notes: Low-profile investor; no published personal or firm contact found. Third-party profiles (MarketScreener) say he started as a senior accountant at Deloitte & Touche and studied at UMBC, but these weren't confirmed in a primary source. Appears in 2024 DFIN proxy but not the 2026 nominee list.

name: William H Lamb
current_role: Independent Director, The Bancorp, Inc. (TBBK); Of Counsel, Lamb McErlane PC (West Chester, PA)
profile: William H. Lamb is a founding partner of West Chester, PA law firm Lamb McErlane and a former Justice of the Supreme Court of Pennsylvania (2003-04). He has been an independent director of fintech-focused bank The Bancorp since around 2004 and now serves Of Counsel in the firm's appellate group, running a mock-argument service for lawyers preparing appeals.
interesting_fact: Appointed to the Pennsylvania Supreme Court by Gov. Mark Schweiker in 2003, he was the first justice from Chester County in 147 years, and was named Chester County Citizen of the Year for it.
deep_cut_fact: As a Chester County special prosecutor (1981-84) he won two Awards of Merit from the Pennsylvania State Police; he served as Chester County DA 1972-80, holds a Duke BA in English and a Penn Law JD cum laude, and sat on the President's Advisory Committee on the Arts.
notes: Addressed as 'Justice Lamb'. Law-firm bio publishes his work email. Recipient of The Legal Intelligencer's 2014 Lifetime Achievement Award. Long-time Bancorp director (since ~2003/04; start year varies by source).

name: Lara Caimi
current_role: President, Worldwide Field Operations, Samsara Inc. (IOT); Director, Aurora Innovation (AUR)
profile: Lara Caimi runs global sales and field operations at connected-operations/IoT company Samsara, which she joined in 2023 reporting to CEO Sanjit Biswas. She previously was ServiceNow's Chief Strategy Officer and then Chief Customer and Partner Officer (2017-2023) after 14 years at Bain & Company, where she was a San Francisco partner advising tech companies. She also sits on the board of self-driving-truck company Aurora and was formerly on Confluent's board.
interesting_fact: She succeeded Andy McCall at Samsara in 2023 and oversees go-to-market for a company selling AI-powered operations tools to fleets, utilities and field-service organizations, an energy/physical-infrastructure angle for the podcast.
deep_cut_fact: She studied Economics and English Literature at St. Olaf College, earned a Master of International Business at the University of Sydney as a Fulbright Scholar, and got her MBA at Harvard; early in her career she was an analyst at Halpern, Denny & Co.
notes: Current title at Samsara confirmed through 2023 announcement and org listings; no 2026 change found. She has spoken on a Thoughtworks podcast about customer success, so she is podcast-friendly. Best route: Samsara media relations.
